name: Drew Durbin
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Wave Mobile Money (Dakar, Senegal)
profile: American entrepreneur who co-founded remittance app Sendwave (YC, sold to WorldRemit for ~$500M in 2020) and then Wave, a low-fee mobile money network that launched in Senegal and became Francophone Africa's first unicorn after a $200M Series A in 2021. He continues to run Wave as it expands across West Africa.
interesting_fact: Wave's flat 1% transfer fee undercut incumbents by roughly 70%, forcing Orange Money and others to slash their prices; Wave reached about 70% of Senegal's mobile-money users.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Sendwave came from his own frustration with fees and unreliable transfers when sending money to an NGO he ran in Tanzania; he and co-founder Lincoln Quirk met as freshman hallmates at Brown University.
notes: Low public profile; no published press email found on wave.com. Best route is via Wave corporate channels.

name: Wu Shufan
current_role: Co-founder/board member, LandSpace; founder and chairman, MinoSpace; Chair Professor and Executive Dean, School of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
profile: Chinese aerospace engineer who co-founded LandSpace in 2015 with Zhang Changwu (CEO) and Wang Jianmeng; LandSpace builds the Zhuque methane-fuelled rockets and is pursuing a Shanghai IPO. He also founded small-satellite maker MinoSpace in 2017 and leads SJTU's aerospace school.
interesting_fact: Wu spent about 17 years in European aerospace research, including 2002-2013 at the European Space Agency's ESTEC centre in the Netherlands, before returning to China.
deep_cut_fact: Before going commercial he was chief engineer of the China-French SVOM gamma-ray-burst science satellite and the STU-2 CubeSat mission at the Shanghai Engineering Centre for Microsatellites (2013-2017); he was also a Humboldt Foundation fellow at TU Braunschweig.
notes: Not the founder/CEO of LandSpace (that is Zhang Changwu); he is a co-founder. Academic route via SJTU School of Aeronautics and Astronautics may be most accessible.

name: Rajesh Ramanand
profile: Payments-risk veteran who co-founded Signifyd with Michael Liberty in 2011 after leading emerging-markets risk at PayPal. Signifyd sells guaranteed-fraud-protection and commerce-protection software to online retailers and reached unicorn status; Ramanand still leads it as CEO.
interesting_fact: Signifyd's model guarantees merchants against chargebacks on orders it approves, shifting fraud liability from the retailer to Signifyd.
deep_cut_fact: Before PayPal he spent years at FedEx working on payments and shipping risk; at Signifyd's 2013 launch he argued that 'a lot of merchants are declining good transactions' because of mismatched identity data.
notes: Goes by 'Raj'. Speaks at Signifyd's FLOW summit and on podcasts; no published press email found on signifyd.com.

name: Steven Goldfeder
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Offchain Labs (now branded Offchain), developer of Arbitrum
profile: Computer scientist who earned a Princeton PhD in cryptocurrency security and, after a Cornell Tech/IC3 postdoc, co-founded Offchain Labs in 2018 with Ed Felten and Harry Kalodner to commercialise the Arbitrum research project. Arbitrum became the largest Ethereum layer-2 rollup; he continues to lead the company as CEO.
interesting_fact: Arbitrum began as an academic research project at Princeton before being spun out as Offchain Labs, which raised at a $1.2B valuation in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: As a Princeton PhD student advised by Arvind Narayanan, he co-authored the widely used textbook 'Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies' (Princeton University Press) alongside Narayanan, Bonneau, Felten and Miller.
notes: Frequent podcast guest (Bankless, Castle Island, Fintech Blueprint) - receptive to long-form interviews.

name: Stuart Kelly
current_role: Co-founder of Zego (technical co-founder, formerly CTO); current title not confirmed
profile: London software engineer who co-founded insurtech Zego in 2016 with Harry Franks and Sten Saar, all ex-onefinestay. As technical co-founder he built the platform that prices pay-as-you-go insurance for gig-economy drivers by the hour; Zego reached a $1.1B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: Zego's first-ever sale was a £2.30 policy, sold after Kelly finished the mobile app in under four months.
deep_cut_fact: He created Zego's proprietary software that uses algorithms to assess a new driver's risk and spin up fresh policies by the hour - the 'secret sauce' behind its gig-worker cover.
notes: Very low public profile; engineer rather than public-facing exec. Some listings say he moved from CTO to a principal/staff engineer role. Co-founders Franks/Saar are more media-facing.

name: Di Weijie
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Flash Express / Flash Group (Thailand)
profile: Chinese technologist who spent over eight years at Alibaba before co-founding Bangkok courier Flash Express with Komsan Saelee in 2017-18. Flash grew to more than 1 million parcels a day across all 77 Thai provinces and became Thailand's first logistics unicorn; Di leads technology and operations.
interesting_fact: Within about two years of launch Flash Express was delivering over 1 million parcels a day from 5,000+ branches, becoming Thailand's second-largest private express carrier.
deep_cut_fact: At Techsauce Global Summit 2025 he said Flash has run its workforce through its own software since day one and that he believes 'the future belongs to small teams or even single individuals' adept at AI.
notes: Komsan Saelee (CEO) is the public face; Di appears at Thai tech conferences such as Techsauce. Only customer-service emails are published.

name: Jeroen Bekaert
current_role: Co-founder and President, Orca Bio (since May 2025; previously COO)
profile: Belgian-born engineer (Ghent PhD in computer science engineering, Stanford GSB master's) who co-founded cell-therapy company Orca Bio in 2016 with Ivan Dimov and Nate Fernhoff. Orca's high-precision cell therapy Orca-T won FDA approval as Tregzi in June 2026 for blood-cancer patients undergoing stem-cell transplants; Bekaert oversees company operations as President.
interesting_fact: Orca-T (Tregzi), approved by the FDA on 30 June 2026, is described as the first regulatory T-cell therapy approved for blood-cancer patients undergoing allogeneic stem-cell transplant.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a researcher at Los Alamos National Laboratory, later ran J&J supply-chain engineering for EMEA and Merck KGaA's Silicon Valley innovation center, and was a Gustave Boel-Sofina Fellow.
notes: Operations-focused executive with a low media profile; Nate Fernhoff is CEO since 2025. Corporate comms contact listed on press releases.

name: Sophie Hersan
current_role: Co-founder and Fashion Director, Vestiaire Collective
profile: French co-founder of Vestiaire Collective, the Paris-born luxury resale marketplace launched in 2009 by six partners including Fanny Moizant. As fashion director she shapes curation and authentication standards; the company reached unicorn status in 2021. After Moizant's January 2026 exit she is reported as the remaining original co-founder still at the company.
interesting_fact: Vestiaire Collective was conceived in a small Parisian apartment by Hersan and five partners in 2009 as a reaction to fashion consumers 'buying more and wearing less'.
deep_cut_fact: Born and raised in France's Champagne region, she earned a degree in economic science before switching to fashion, and grew up idolizing Azzedine Alaia, Claude Montana, Thierry Mugler and Karl Lagerfeld.
notes: Media-friendly on sustainability/circular fashion topics (frequent interviews). No dedicated press email found on Vestiaire's site.

name: Bhavin Pandya
profile: Indian entrepreneur who co-founded Games24x7 in 2006 with Trivikraman Thampy after both studied economics at NYU. The company built RummyCircle and fantasy-sports app My11Circle, applying data science to gaming, and reached a $2.5B valuation backed by Tiger Global; it also runs a venture arm and a foundation.
interesting_fact: Pandya describes Games24x7 as 'a technology platform, gaming is just incidental' - the company brands itself around 'The Science of Gaming' and serves 120M+ players.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Trivikraman Thampy met while studying economics at New York University and bonded over a shared passion for online games; Pandya returned to India in 2006 to start the company. He also holds an electrical and computer engineering degree from Purdue.
notes: India's 2025 online-gaming law banned real-money games, forcing a major business pivot for Games24x7 - context worth knowing but handle tactfully. Purdue degree comes from a secondary profile (theofficialboard).

name: Tom Okman
current_role: Co-founder of Nord Security (NordVPN) and Tesonet; co-founder of enterprise AI platform nexos.ai
profile: Lithuanian entrepreneur (Tomas Okmanas, b. 1987, Vilnius) who co-founded tech accelerator Tesonet in 2008 and NordVPN in 2012 with Eimantas Sabaliauskas, later grouping it into Nord Security (NordVPN, NordPass, NordLayer), valued at $3B in 2023. In 2025 he launched nexos.ai, which raised a $35M Series A at a $350M valuation.
interesting_fact: He is a named inventor on a US patent for a method that cuts the time TCP packets take to travel between a VPN client, server and destination.
deep_cut_fact: He studied history at Vilnius University; at Tesonet he and Sabaliauskas tried 34 projects and ideas - from computer games to web hosting - before focusing on network security. He says the nexos.ai idea came to him on 28 Oct 2024 and the product was ready in 30 days.
notes: Also known as Tomas Okmanas. Named a National Patron of Lithuania for Ukraine fundraising; Forbes Technology Council member. AI angle (nexos.ai) is a natural podcast hook.

name: Tomy Pelluz
current_role: Co-founder of Domestika (listed by Hurun); listed as Domestika staff on the platform - current title not confirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Domestika, the creative-skills online course platform that began as an online forum and showcase for creative professionals and is now headquartered in Berkeley, California. Further biographical details could not be verified in this pass.
interesting_fact: Domestika started as an online forum and showcase for creative professionals before becoming one of the largest online course platforms for creatives.
notes: Research incomplete: web-search budget ran out; only company pages were checked. His Domestika profile (@pelluz) is marked Staff and lists Barcelona, Spain. Needs a follow-up pass.

name: Deepak Khetan
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of GlobalBees, an Indian house-of-brands roll-up that became a unicorn in December 2021. GlobalBees' own site credits Nitin Agarwal and Supam Maheshwari as co-founders and lists Anuj Jain as CEO; Deepak Khetan does not appear on its About, Board or Executive pages, so his link to the company could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: GlobalBees reached unicorn status in December 2021, its first year, among the fastest Indian startups to do so.
notes: Identity unverified - possibly a Hurun attribution error or an early/departed co-founder. Web-search budget ran out before this could be resolved; needs follow-up. Contact listed is the company's general inbox, not his.

name: Liu Baiqi
current_role: Co-founder (with Xia Dongkun) and chief executive, Galactic Energy (Beijing), per company/Wikipedia founder listings
profile: Chinese aerospace entrepreneur who co-founded private launch company Galactic Energy in Beijing E-Town in February 2018 with Xia Dongkun; the founding team were senior engineers from China's state space system. Galactic flies the solid-fuel Ceres-1 rocket and is developing the reusable liquid-fuelled Pallas-1 and Ceres-2.
interesting_fact: In December 2021 Galactic Energy became the first Chinese private company to reach orbit twice; the company's stated long-term goal is mining asteroids for rare metals and minerals.
notes: Exact current title (CEO vs chairman) not independently confirmed; personal biography not verified because web-search budget ran out. Company slogan: 'Let space resources enter daily life' (让太空资源融入生活).

name: Chrisna Aditya
current_role: Former co-founder and Chief Product Officer, eFishery (resigned in 2024-25)
profile: Indonesian co-founder and former chief product officer of eFishery, the Bandung aquaculture-tech company founded in 2013 that built IoT automated fish-feeding systems and became a unicorn in 2023. He resigned after a 2024 audit found the company's figures had been heavily overstated, primarily attributed to the then-CEO; the company was subsequently wound down.
interesting_fact: eFishery's core product was an IoT smart feeder that adjusted feed doses in fish and shrimp ponds to reduce waste and detect pond problems.
notes: Sensitive: eFishery collapsed after an accounting-fraud audit (Wikipedia). Founder/CEO Gibran Huzaifah is under investigation; Chrisna resigned. Likely not a suitable or receptive outreach target; no current public role or published contact found.

name: Lukasz Osipiuk
current_role: Co-founder and Senior Staff Software Engineer, Starburst; Trino project maintainer
profile: Polish software engineer listed among Starburst's founders, the company Justin Borgman started in 2017 out of Teradata's Presto team to commercialise the open-source distributed SQL engine now called Trino. Starburst sells data-lakehouse/federated query software and was valued at $3.35B in 2022; Osipiuk remains a hands-on engineer rather than an executive.
interesting_fact: Starburst's founding team came from Teradata, which had acquired Borgman's 'SQL on Hadoop' startup Hadapt in 2014; Starburst was founded in 2017 to build on the Presto (now Trino) engine originally created at Facebook.
deep_cut_fact: He is one of the officially listed maintainers of the open-source Trino SQL query engine (GitHub handle 'losipiuk'), alongside Presto's original Facebook creators Martin Traverso, Dain Sundstrom and David Phillips.
notes: Engineer, not a public-facing exec; engaging via Trino community (Slack/GitHub, Trino Summit) may be more natural than corporate PR. CEO Justin Borgman is Starburst's spokesperson.

name: Evan Rosenbaum
current_role: Co-founder, Genies (Los Angeles AI avatar company); current title not confirmed
profile: University of Pennsylvania alum who co-founded Genies with CEO Akash Nigam in 2017 after their earlier app Blend. Genies builds AI avatars and companion characters for celebrities, brands and developers, has raised about $250M from investors including Silver Lake, Bond and Bob Iger (who joined its board in 2022), and has partnered with Unity, Sanrio and the NBA players' union.
interesting_fact: Genies' avatars were adopted by stars such as Justin Bieber, Shawn Mendes and Russell Westbrook, and Bob Iger joined its board in March 2022 right after leaving Disney.
deep_cut_fact: Before Genies, he and Nigam (who met while at Penn and Michigan respectively) raised a seed round for a group-chat app called Blend, building it from a tiny room attached to a mosque in San Jose; they turned down a weak exit offer and pivoted its tech into Genies.
notes: Made Forbes 30 Under 30 (Consumer Tech) with Nigam (per Los Altos Town Crier, 2019). Akash Nigam is the public face; Rosenbaum keeps a low profile.
